name: Dynamic Array Usage
description: Use ArrayList or vector-style indexed storage, resizing expectations, and linear traversal habits confidently in DSA code.
exampleJava: for (int i = 1; i < nums.length; i++) nums[i] += nums[i - 1];
commonMistakes: Rebuilding arrays unnecessarily instead of updating in place
Mixing index math and loop boundaries

name: String Builder Usage
description: Use StringBuilder or mutable string accumulation patterns instead of slow repeated immutable concatenation.
commonMistakes: Concatenating immutable strings inside long loops
Forgetting to append the leftover suffix after one string ends

name: Hash Map Usage
description: Use HashMap or unordered_map style counting and lookup patterns to model frequencies and presence checks.
commonMistakes: Reading a missing key without a default value
Updating only one side of a frequency comparison

name: Stack Library Usage
description: Use stack-like library operations cleanly for push, pop, peek, and last-kept-element simulation.
exampleJava: if (!stack.isEmpty() && stack.peek() == ch) stack.pop(); else stack.push(ch);
commonMistakes: Using the wrong end of the container as the top

name: Queue Library Usage
description: Use queue-style APIs for FIFO processing, front access, and query simulation without shifting full arrays manually.
commonMistakes: Using remove(0) on a dynamic array instead of a queue structure

name: Priority Queue Usage
description: Use min-heaps or max-heaps correctly for top-k and best-first maintenance patterns.
commonMistakes: Choosing a max-heap when the pattern needs a min-heap of size k
Forgetting to evict elements when the heap grows past the intended size

name: Collection Iteration Usage
description: Move comfortably between arrays, strings, maps, stacks, queues, and heaps while keeping loops and temporary state under control.
exampleJava: for (int value : nums) { if (heap.size() < k) heap.offer(value); }
commonMistakes: Nesting extra loops because container traversal feels unfamiliar
Using incompatible container operations for the required access pattern
